ADVENTURE CREATOR / SKILLS: NATIVE SKILL TEXT PRODUCERS

Source images are the two paths configured by data/runtime/native-pe-images.json.
The source extraction reads their on-disk instructions and data. It does not
load either image into a game process. All addresses below are RVAs.

reference PE:6a70a6d9:02711000
classic   PE:6a70b91c:0270a000

The following are distinct native domains, despite sharing English words:
  * archetype labels: eligible preset.skill -> profession-style skill title;
  * customized skill rows: a rating and profession-style title in one string;
  * skill tooltip heading: the plain skill noun, without race/caste overrides;
  * skill tooltip explanation: a skill-id switch in the creator renderer;
  * attribute tooltip skill lists: the same plain skill noun;
  * dynamic RAW profession titles: selected race/caste NativeStrings;
  * dynamic weapon skill availability: selected RAW weapon definitions.

The assembly files and skill-native-branches.tsv retain each exact selector,
branch address, literal operand and source spelling separately for both PEs.
The enum_metadata column names are only descriptive metadata from the existing
df-structures source; the selector-to-branch mappings come from the PE tables.

1. RATING ATOMS AND ONE-STRING SKILL ROWS

rating_text(out, int level):
  out.clear()
  switch (uint32(level)) {
    0: "Dabbling"
    1: "Novice"
    2: "Adequate"
    3: "Competent"
    4: "Skilled"
    5: "Proficient"
    6: "Talented"
    7: "Adept"
    8: "Expert"
    9: "Professional"
   10: "Accomplished"
   11: "Great"
   12: "Master"
   13: "High Master"
   14: "Grand Master"
   default: "Legendary"
  }

reference body 7737c0..77394c, table 77394c
classic   body 7711e0..77136c, table 77136c

The customized skill row constructs its rating in a temporary NativeString,
appends a space, obtains the title in another NativeString, and appends that
title before the single row draw. Native zero-total handling supplies "Not"
instead of calling rating_text. The level source is the sum of the selected
skill's creator+0x7c+4*skill and creator+0x34c+4*skill fields. Source fragments
are not independent messages; for example the semantic row is the whole
"Competent Knife User", with one skill/rating result and one suppression span.

reference row call 629af7 -> 7737c0; 629b66 -> 774730
classic   corresponding row calls use 7711e0 and 772150

2. PROFESSION-STYLE SKILL TITLES, INCLUDING RAW OVERRIDES

skill_title(out, int16 skill, int16 race, int16 caste):
  profession = skill_to_profession(skill)
  if profession != -1 and has_raw_singular_profession(race, caste, profession):
    raw_profession(out, race, caste, profession, plural=false, capitalize=true)
    return
  out.clear()
  switch (uint32(skill)) {
    0..146: native skill-specific case
    default: return empty
  }

The complete 147-case static title inventory is in skill-native-branches.tsv
under role=title. It includes the weapon users, arts, social skills, trades,
medical skills and "Skill 1" through "Skill 10". The text is the title helper's
native spelling, rather than an inferred spelling based on screenshots.

reference body 774730..775284, case table 775284
classic   body 772150..772ca4, case table 772ca4

At reference 774756 / classic 772176 the helper maps the skill to a profession
enum. The map is itself a PE selector: reference 764a70..764c74, branch table
764c74 and byte permutation 764db0; classic 762490..762694, branch table
762694 and byte permutation 7627d0. A mapped -1 disables the RAW override.

At reference 774773 / classic 772193 the availability gate reads the selected
race's caste vector. It tests the SINGULAR string length:
  caste+0x1830+32*profession first, then race+0x230+32*profession.
An unavailable/invalid caste may still use the race string.

At reference 77479e / classic 7721be the successful override invokes the RAW
title selector with plural=false and capitalize=true. In the caller those
arguments are stack+0x28 = 0 and stack+0x30 = 1. The actual source operand is:
  caste+0x1820+32*profession,
  falling back to race+0x220+32*profession when the caste string is empty.
The plural arrays at caste+0x2900 and race+0x1300 are not selected by this
Skills title call. Capitalization only uppercases an ASCII first letter.

reference availability 30cea0..30cf63; source selector 30cf70..30d0e4
classic   availability 30aa60..30ab23; source selector 30ab30..30aca4

The Fisherman fallback case additionally reads race+0x6e0 (length+0x6f0)
before its literal "Fisherman". This is the same race singular array entry
for profession 0x26/FISHERMAN, not another free text token.

The page passes creator race+0x78 and caste+0x7a to this helper for skill rows
and archetype labels. RAWs can therefore produce "Axedwarf", "Hammerdwarf",
"Speardwarf", "Marksdwarf", "Swordsdwarf", "Macedwarf", "Pikedwarf" and
"Bowdwarf" rather than the general English titles. Fresh configured-install
source operands, exact tokens and file/line provenance are in
skill-raw-profession-sources.tsv. Future mod RAW strings remain typed dynamic
source operands rather than a finite PE literal enumeration.

3. PLAIN SKILL NOUNS

skill_noun(out, int16 skill):
  out.clear()
  if uint32(skill) > 136: return
  out = native_case_table[skill]

reference body 773990..77450c, table 77450c
classic   body 7713b0..771f2c, table 771f2c

All 137 noun selectors are retained under role=noun in the branch TSV.
These are a different domain from titles: Axe/Axeman, Lash/Lasher,
Wrestling/Wrestler, Poetry/Poet, Speaking/Speaker, Reading/Reader, etc.
The tooltip call reference 62a975 -> 773990 does not pass race or caste and
cannot return PROFESSION_NAME overrides. Attribute tooltips also invoke
this same noun producer for their "Affects skills:" lists.

4. ALL SKILL TOOLTIP DESCRIPTION BRANCHES

description_for_skill(skill):
  if uint32(skill - 2) <= 0x84:
    branch = descriptions[permutation[skill - 2]]
  else:
    branch = default_description
  append_wrapped_description(branch.literal, native_width=0x30)

reference selector 62a99e..62a9c7; branch table 634c3c; permutation 634cd0
classic   selector 6283be..6283e7; branch table 63265c; permutation 6326f0

The TSV role=description maps every skill id through the exact native selector,
including the fallback:
  "Not useful unless you retire and subsequently become a resident in Fortress mode."
This is native fallback text and remains a whole tooltip explanation.

Shared branches include:
  Weapon users -> "Weapon skill."
  Fighting -> charging and own/enemy combat opportunities.
  Archery -> partially replaces low ranged skills.
  Observation -> traps, ambushers, charge defense, enemy attack information.
  Swimming -> safe swimming without floundering.
  Climbing -> difficult surfaces.
  Ambush -> remaining hidden while sneaking.
  Tracking -> tracks and spoor.
  Riding -> mounted opportunities and ranged accuracy.
  Discipline -> pain and stress.
  Shield -> blocking melee and ranged attacks.
  Armor -> movement and dodging while armored.
  Dodging -> dodging melee and ranged attacks.
  Wrestling -> wrestling and charging.
  Striking/Kicking/Biting -> the corresponding appendage attacks.
  Throwing -> throwing objects.
  Misc. Object -> weapons outside other skill domains.
  Knapping -> making a sharp rock using two rocks.
  Woodcutting -> requiring an item with a sharp edge.
  Craft skill group -> "Crafting skill."
  Reading -> a novice level is required to read anything.
  Writing -> minor effect on both poetry and prose.
  Prose/Poetry -> quality of the corresponding writing form.
  Speaking -> poetry recitals, preaching, storytelling, musical forms.
  Music -> partially replaces low musical performance skills.
  Dance/Singing/instrument group -> "Performance skill."
  Leadership -> maximum number of followers.
  Persuasion -> stating values, arguments, interrogation persuasion.
  Intimidation -> argument dismissal and interrogation intimidation.
  Judging Intent -> emotional states during conversations.
  Comedy/Flattery/Consoling/Pacification -> their respective native clauses.

These summaries are explanatory only. Exact native wording is in the source
literal/branch TSVs, preserving existing spelling such as "affect" in
"Has a minor affect on all writing (poetry and prose.)".

Following the explanation, reference 62b212 / classic 628c32 obtains three
physical attribute ids and three mental attribute ids and emits
"Affected by attributes:" followed by their names. Id -1 is skipped. Slot zero has no
suffix; slots one and two append " (minor)" at reference 62b2a4/62b3a7
(classic 628cc4/628dc7). These are ordered importance slots, not numerical
weights. Attribute tooltips reverse the relationship and emit "Affects skills:"
or "Affects no skills.". Their dynamic list entries use skill_noun,
not skill_title.

5. ARCHETYPES: 20 ELIGIBLE SKILL PRESETS AND BLANK SLATE

The builder reads the ordered creator+0x1200 vector of available skills.
For each skill, a PE switch either builds a preset or advances without one:
  37 38 39 40 41 42 49 50 -> melee preset
  43 51 52                -> ranged preset
  99                      -> wrestler preset
  90                      -> poet preset
  92                      -> speaker preset
  116                     -> dancer preset
  118 119 120 121 122     -> singing/instrument preset
Every other available skill is skipped by this preset switch. The builder
always appends a preset with NativeString literal "Blank slate".

reference body 63fa00..641008; branch table 641008; permutation 641028
classic   body 63d420..63ea28; branch table 63ea28; permutation 63ea48

Preset+0x20 records its skill id. The row renderer obtains the preset from
creator+0x1220; a nonnegative skill id uses skill_title with creator race/caste.
Preset+0x20 == -1 instead copies the preset NativeString (Blank slate).
The displayed label subsequently passes the native capitalization helper.
Thus the total possible static preset labels are the twenty role titles plus
Blank slate, subject to which skills the selected background makes available.
Their actual display order follows the ordered availability vector, explaining
why the screenshot starts Lasher rather than the ascending skill enum.

6. CUSTOM SKILL AVAILABILITY AND ITS DYNAMIC RAW OPERANDS

Availability preparation belongs to a different native method from rendering:
  reference input segment 5ca198..5ca5b2
  classic   input segment 5c7bb8..5c7fd2

If creator+0x2d0 == -1 (no selected background entity):
  clear creator+0x1200
  for weapon in world RAW weapon definitions:
    if weapon.ranged_skill(+0xd2) != -1:
      append_unique(weapon.ranged_skill)
    elif weapon.melee_skill(+0xd0) != -1:
      append_unique(weapon.melee_skill)
  append the explicit fixed skill sequence recorded in skill-text-productions.tsv
  include Swimming (69) only when selected race flag0x56 is true
  build_archetypes(creator, selected_character_type)

If a background entity is selected:
  entity = native entity lookup(creator+0x2d0)
  entity_available_skills(entity, creator+0x1200)
  build_archetypes(creator, selected_character_type)

reference entity helper 93cef0..93deca
classic   entity helper 93a720..93b6fa

The entity helper first walks weapon ids in entity+0x148/+0x150 and reads the
same RAW weapon fields with ranged-before-melee precedence. It then appends
its native skill sequence and uses the entity's selected race for Swimming.
The 0x56 flag is HAS_ANY_CAN_SWIM in the existing enum metadata.

append_unique(reference 641c10..641c58; classic 63f630..63f678) compares
int16 skill ids and preserves first occurrence order; it adds no text.
Configured installation ITEM_WEAPON SKILL/RANGED operands, their exact RAW
tokens and file/line sources are in skill-raw-weapon-sources.tsv. A mod can
alter available weapon skill ids and profession title strings without adding
new static English strings to the creator renderer.
